headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because ms-swift reads/writes files and calls external APIs while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no ingestion path, so it cannot directly inject B. B does read files/stdin and can process CLI/Python inputs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or provenance bridge. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file handoff, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B's stdin or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced later, B may parse attacker-controlled content from A.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting A outputs into B prompts.
Require a human review step before B consumes any A-produced text.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared mount between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write files and sends requests to allowlisted external APIs, while A is a docs-only artifact with no runtime protections or isolation. If both are placed in the same workspace, B can ingest files that may contain sensitive material and transmit them to third-party inference backends. A does not mitigate this path.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or mounted workspace, B can read A-associated files.
IF those files contain secrets, logs, or datasets, B may upload their contents to external APIs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Remove secrets from any shared folder before running B.
Set B to offline mode where possible.
Restrict B's API credentials to non-sensitive test data.
Review allowlisted endpoints before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write and shell/subprocess execution, while A is non-runnable and therefore cannot contend for resources itself. The conflict arises if an orchestrator places both against the same mutable directory or artifacts; then B can overwrite files A references. Because shared-state isolation is not stated, uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, B can overwrite shared artifacts.
IF an orchestrator reuses filenames across runs, B may clobber A-related outputs.
mitigations: Assign unique output directories per agent.
Run B with a read-only mount for A artifacts.
Use timestamped filenames for generated outputs.
Check for existing files before launching B.
Add a manual lock on any shared workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on files and API outputs, so if it consumes A-derived text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work. A is only an awesome-list repo and cannot verify facts at runtime, while B's CLI/Python workflow can operationalize whatever it is given. No built-in verification or provenance tracking is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text as source material without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF B is configured to generate reports or training artifacts from A outputs, those errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require source verification before B acts on A output.
Insert a human review checkpoint between A and B.
Keep A outputs as reference-only, not authoritative input.
Log provenance for any text passed from A to B.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class or residency mismatch is documented for either agent, and A touches no data classes at runtime. B does handle secrets and multiple data classes, but the profile does not state a jurisdictional or certification mismatch. This is therefore a compliance-overlap concern with documented gaps, not a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into B's workflows, compliance review is required.
IF B's allowlisted APIs are outside the operator's approved residency or retention policy, a mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Classify the data before use.
Keep regulated data out of B until policy is confirmed.
Review B's API destinations and retention settings.
Document the approved residency for each dataset.
Escalate any PHI or EU PII workflow to compliance review.
